newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo port '96 transshipment traffic up 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Colombo port '96 transshipment traffic up 40 pct.

text.p: Transshipment traffic at Colombo port rose 40 percent to 979,882 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) last year from 700,000 containers in 1995, according to provisional figures in the Central Bank's 1996 annual report.
Transshipment as a percentage of container traffic throughput rose to 72 percent from 67 percent over the same period, said the report released on Wednesday.
Transshipment occurs when a vessel discharges cargo at an intermediate port and the goods are unloaded to another ship bound for the final destination.
The port handled a record 1.4 million containers last year, up 29 percent from 1995, Sri Lanka Ports Authority chairman Ranjit Wickramasinghe said on Monday.
The Central Bank report said Colombo port's revenue rose 82 percent to 8.3 million rupees ($140 million) in 1996 from 4.6 billion rupees in 1995.
